title: Design decisions: federated user mention textual form
description:
Make the design decisions for the textual `@user@host` form for federated user mentions, BEFORE any spec edits in Epic f13f.

Blocked on jmap-chat-spec-fig9.2 (main draft must have the Mention type discriminator infrastructure in place).

---

DECISION 1 — Textual form

`@alice@example.com` (ActivityPub / Mastodon convention) is the obvious default. Alternatives: `@alice%example.com`, `@alice/example.com`, etc. ActivityPub-style is the strong default.

---

DECISION 2 — Wire representation

The Mention type (post-Epic-A) carries `type` and conditional `id`. For federated user mentions, options:
- `type: "user"`, `id: "alice@example.com"` — the federated form goes into the existing `id` field
- `type: "user"`, `id: "<local-contact-id>"`, `federatedHandle: "alice@example.com"` — separate field for the textual form
- New scope value: `type: "federated-user"`, with a distinct field

The current rich-body example at draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md:1296 already shows `userId: "user:alice@example.com"`. That suggests Option 1 is the existing implicit convention.

---

DECISION 3 — Client-side textual parsing

Should clients pattern-match `@user@host` strings in the body and resolve them, or rely on structured Mention entries from the sender's client?

The spec already uses structured mentions (offset/length annotations) for the textual form. Clients composing a message attach Mention entries; clients reading a message render from the Mention entries. This works for federated mentions too — the sender's client resolves the textual form and attaches the Mention.

Question: does the spec need to say anything about parsing textual `@user@host` strings, or is the structured-mention pattern sufficient?

Recommendation: stay with structured. Don't standardize pattern-matching.

---

DECISION 4 — Resolution mechanism

When the sender types `@alice@example.com` in their client, how does the client resolve `example.com` to a ChatContact / federation peer?

- Look up an existing ChatContact whose federation peer is `example.com`?
- Perform `/.well-known/jmap` discovery to find a federation peer?
- Maintain a local cache of known peers and their users?

This is the federation contact-resolution gap mentioned in the parent epic description. May require federation draft changes (a Peer/resolveContact method?) or may be left to client implementations.

---

Open questions to resolve here:
- Confirm or override each recommendation
- Whether resolution requires a new federation method or stays client-side
- Whether validation of the federated form happens at send time or accept time
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the four decisions has a documented chosen answer
- The wire representation is unambiguous enough that jmap-chat-spec-f13f.2 (main draft implementation) can begin
- The resolution mechanism is either deferred to clients or specified well enough to file as a federation-draft bead
close_reason: All four design decisions made in collaborative session: textual forms = @user@host + DID URI; wire form = type='user' with id; parsing and resolution both deployment-defined.
